candidates.source_name: CBCG — Finansijski izvještaji banaka (bank financial statements repository)
candidates.why_relevant: Compulsory central repository of per-bank audited annual and unaudited quarterly financial statements (balance sheet, P&L, cash flow, equity, notes, management commentary, auditor opinion). Page content observed listing PDF annual reports and ZIP quarterly filings for individual banks with coverage roughly 2011-2025. This is the single richest per-institution disclosure archive in Montenegro.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of the per-bank sub-pages, harvest PDF/ZIP links into a versioned document store; parse PDFs downstream. Quarterly cadence (filings land ~45-90 days after quarter end), plus an annual sweep for audited reports.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + direct fetch of CBCG supervision section
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore godišnji izvještaj bankarski sektor
cbcg.me "Izvještaj o stanju u bankarskom sistemu Crne Gore" kvartalni

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Bilansi stanja i bilansi uspjeha banaka (bank balance sheets & income statements)
candidates.why_relevant: Standardised supervisory-template balance sheet and income statement data per bank, published by the regulator itself — far easier to normalise into a time series than PDF annual reports, and comparable across all licensed banks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl; download XLS/PDF tables and load into a per-bank metrics table keyed on institution + period.
queries_used: cbcg.me "Izvještaj o stanju u bankarskom sistemu Crne Gore" kvartalni

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (register of licensed banks)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to the full population of licensed banks (observed ~12 active: CKB, Hipotekarna, Prva banka, Erste, NLB, Addiko, Universal Capital Bank, Lovćen banka, Zapad banka, Ziraat Montenegro, Adriatic Bank, Podgorička banka). Each entry has its own sub-page with licence details and links onward to that bank's own IR/website — the seed list for every downstream actor-level crawl.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of register + per-bank sub-pages; diff to detect new licences, withdrawals, mergers, name changes. Use as the canonical entity list for entity resolution.
queries_used: CBCG registar banaka i platnih institucija licencirane institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata (payment institutions register)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory register of licensed payment institutions and their agents under the Zakon o platnom prometu — the definitive map of non-bank PSP competition in Montenegro and a seed list for company-level tracking.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl with diffing on entity list; feed new entrants into an alerting queue.
queries_used: CBCG registar banaka i platnih institucija licencirane institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata (e-money institutions register)
candidates.why_relevant: Definitive list of licensed e-money issuers and their agents — the fintech/EMI layer of the Montenegrin payments market.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl + diff alongside the payment institutions register.
queries_used: CBCG registar banaka i platnih institucija licencirane institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (payment systems register)
candidates.why_relevant: Lists the payment systems authorised/operated in Montenegro (RTGS, DNS, and any card/instant schemes) — infrastructure-level map for payments market entry analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl + diff.
queries_used: CBCG registar banaka i platnih institucija licencirane institucije

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registri (payments registers hub)

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Statistika Platnog sistema Centralne banke Crne Gore (RTGS/DNS/IPS payment system statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Observed page publishes transaction counts and values split RTGS vs DNS, average daily volumes, system availability, and (per the page) IPS/instant payments data from July 2026 — the core payments-volume time series for Montenegro, with monthly PDF annexes ('Prilog').
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl; capture page text plus attached PDF tables into a payments-volume time series.

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu (payment services & e-money data)
candidates.why_relevant: ECB-style payment-services statistics (cards, terminals/POS-ATM, credit transfers, direct debits, e-money) — the closest Montenegrin equivalent to ECB Payments Statistics and the key demand-side series for a payments-hardware/software vendor. candidates.why_relevant: Aggregate MFI balance sheet, deposits, loans and interest-rate series compiled on ECB/IMF methodology and published monthly — the backbone macro-banking dataset for sizing the Montenegrin banking market.

negative_findings.description: cbcg.me serves the same content under many differing first path segments (/me/, /r/, /c/, /e/, /en/, /eng/, /images/, /uploads/, /legal/, /discover/, /index/ and even /kursna_lista_arhiva.php/...). Search engines index these variants interchangeably.
negative_findings.result_summary: The same page (e.g. registar banaka, tarife banaka) was returned under at least three different prefixes across searches. A fetch of https://www.cbcg.me/r/mapa-sajta returned HTTP 404 although the sitemap page is indexed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hardcoded deep URLs will rot and produce false 'dead source' verdicts. Collection must resolve links dynamically from section roots, and the verifier should treat a single 404 on a prefixed URL as a prefix problem, not a dead source.

negative_findings.description: No open-data API, SDMX endpoint, or bulk-download facility for CBCG banking/payments data was found in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: All observed outputs are HTML pages plus PDF/ZIP/XLS attachments; no /api, data portal, or SDMX reference surfaced in searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be crawl-and-parse (PDF/XLS extraction), which is slower and more brittle; budget for document parsing rather than API ingestion.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for a CBCG-hosted central repository of bank Pillar 3 disclosures ('objelodanjivanje podataka kreditnih institucija').
negative_findings.result_summary: Found the regulatory basis (Odluka o adekvatnosti kapitala banke; a decision on public disclosure of credit-institution data) but no single CBCG page aggregating banks' Pillar 3 disclosure documents. The obligation appears to sit with each bank's own website.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pillar 3 capital/risk disclosures likely have to be collected bank-by-bank from institution websites (a different coverage cell), not from CBCG. This is a real structural gap, not a search failure.

negative_findings.description: The fetched 'Finansijski izvještaji banaka' page rendered only a subset of institutions (six banks) although the register lists ~12 active banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetch returned CKB, Hipotekarna, Podgorička, Invest banka Montenegro (in liquidation), Prva banka, Erste. NLB, Addiko, Universal Capital, Lovćen, Zapad, Ziraat, Adriatic were not visible in the fetched rendering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Likely pagination/JS rendering rather than missing filings — but a naive single-fetch crawler would silently under-collect. Collection must paginate or render JS and reconcile against the bank register.

negative_findings.description: The payment-services/e-money statistics sub-page URL was inferred from navigation labels observed on the parent statistics page, not directly fetched.
negative_findings.result_summary: Path '/podaci-o-platnim-uslugama-i-elektronskom-novcu' appeared as a navigation sibling; exact absolute URL not confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Flagged with low confidence so the deterministic verification pass resolves the canonical URL from the parent hub rather than assuming it is dead.

coverage_gaps.description: CBCG publishes payment-system volumes (RTGS/DNS/IPS) and, apparently, payment-services statistics, but no card-scheme-level, acquiring-level or POS/ATM-terminal-estate breakdown surfaced in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm the contents of 'Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu' and, if terminal/card counts are absent, cover via bank annual reports, Monstat, and card schemes in other cells; consider an FOI (pristup informacijama) request to CBCG.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell maps CBCG as publisher but not the individual banks'/PSPs' own investor-relations and disclosure pages, which are where Pillar 3 disclosures, shareholder-assembly materials and press releases actually live.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Spawn a per-institution cell seeded from the CBCG Registar banaka and the payment-institution/e-money registers (12+ banks plus PIs/EMIs), plus parent-group IR sites (OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat).

coverage_gaps.description: No non-CBCG archival/mirroring source was identified for withdrawn or superseded CBCG documents; CBCG appears to overwrite or move publication pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Wayback Machine snapshots as a secondary archive for key CBCG pages, and snapshot every downloaded PDF locally with retrieval timestamps.

coverage_gaps.description: The English (/en/) mirror covers publications well but registers, tariffs and statistics appear predominantly Montenegrin-only; some /eng/ paths exist inconsistently.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat sr as the authoritative collection language for registers/tariffs/statistics and en only for flagship publications; budget for sr-language PDF parsing and translation.

coverage_gaps.description: Publication cadence and exact release dates (statistical publication calendar) were referenced but the calendar page itself was not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and track the CBCG 'kalendar objavljivanja statističkih podataka' to schedule collection precisely instead of blind polling.

brief: CBCG (Centralna banka Crne Gore) is effectively the whole primary-source layer for Montenegrin bank disclosure and payments intelligence: it hosts the per-bank financial statements repository (audited annual PDFs and quarterly ZIP filings, roughly 2011-2025), standardised balance-sheet/income-statement tables, the statutory registers of banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment systems, RTGS/DNS/IPS payment-system statistics, monetary and financial-soundness statistics, and an unusually valuable regulator-hosted comparison of bank payment tariffs. Everything is free, public and legally mandated, but delivered as HTML plus PDF/ZIP/XLS attachments with no API, and the site serves identical pages under many rotating path prefixes, so collection should crawl from stable section roots and resolve child links dynamically rather than hardcoding deep URLs. The main structural gap inside this cell is Pillar 3 / 'objelodanjivanje' disclosures, for which the regulation exists but no central CBCG repository was found - those live on individual bank websites and need their own coverage cell seeded from the Registar banaka. Card-scheme and terminal-estate granularity also appears absent and may require the payment-services statistics page or a freedom-of-information request.
